corpus.title: Babylonian exile overview
corpus.text: Jerusalem was captured by Nebuchadnezzar II in 587 BCE. Many inhabitants of Judah were deported to Babylon; this period is known as the Babylonian exile. It ended after the Persian conquest of Babylon in 539 BCE.

corpus.title: Hermetic tradition notes
corpus.text: The Corpus Hermeticum is a collection of Greek texts attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, generally dated by scholars to the first centuries CE rather than to remote antiquity.

corpus.title: Archivum lore: the Ninth Archivist
corpus.text: In the internal canon, the Ninth Archivist hid a copper astrolabe inside the library of Alexandria to guard the forbidden index.

corpus.title: Ptolemaic astronomy
corpus.text: Ptolemy's Almagest described a geocentric model in which the planets move on epicycles. It dominated astronomy until Copernicus proposed a heliocentric model.

corpus.title: Gnostic interpretation essay
corpus.text: Some Gnostic readings interpret the serpent of Eden as a bringer of knowledge rather than a deceiver; this is an interpretation, not a consensus view.
